Situation escalated

Situation defused
Life in our bustling city is not exactly simple, and when you're looking for trouble, you tend to find it.
You'd think that your fellow citizens have better things to do than start arguments in public, but here you are.
An innocent shoulder bump in the crowd unraveled into a dramatic quarrel. How do you react?
Much Ado About Nothing
Settle the matter peacefully
The tension eased, and you parted on calmer terms.
There was an incident in the crowd, but in the end everyone parted on calm terms.
Denounce this shameful behavior
Your words stung, leaving the matter worse than it had started.
Insults were exchanged during an incident in the crowd.
A red-tailed comet blazes across the sky, sparkling lively discussions among common folk, philosophers, and religious figures alike.
Citizens report feeling drained, and all sorts of bad things seem to be happening for no reason, as if an evil has seeped into the city.

Attend

Decline
The working class admire your refusal to succumb to such extravagant delights. It has also spared your pocket.
Some upstart has spurned the city's nobility. Foolish move.

You were minding your own business when a swarm of bees suddenly decided that you were the problem.
There was buzzing, swatting, running, and considerably less dignity than you would care to remember.
You could swear the swarm briefly formed the shape of a giant fist before knocking you flat. No one is going to believe that.

People are talking about the {O_CHA_TOWCOU_C}Town Council's{##} latest efforts to curb crime and heresy.

Supposedly, persons convicted of crimes would be pilloried instead of {ST_CHR_IMP_C}imprisoned{##}, so that the citizens can express their dissatisfaction however they see fit. It would probably also help cut down maintenance costs at the {B_PUB_PRI_C}prison{##}.

If a {B_PUB_PIL_C}pillory{##} has been built in our city, and if these new rules are indeed not mere rumors, there is surely a heckling crowd gathering to chuck a rotten cabbage or two at the convicted. Go search for it so you can join in on the mischief or show your superior virtue and capacity for forgiveness.
Let the Sinless Cast the First Stone
Your family has been blessed with a child! May this new life grow in health, and may your dynasty endure through the ages!
Sleepless nights may follow, but they are a small price for such joy. Plus, nothing worth doing is ever easy.
As your child grows, don't forget to invest in their {A_TRACHI_C}education{##} so that, one day, they can contribute meaningfully to your dynasty and even become your {CHAR_HEI_C}heir{##}.
Come hold the newest member of your dynasty!

Your spouse has already taken the liberty of naming the child after a dearly beloved relative from their side of the family. A touching gesture, no doubt, though they seem rather attached to their choice.

Will you honor their wishes and have the child baptized under that name, or exercise your authority as head of the dynasty and choose one yourself? Just remember, you'll have to share a bed with your spouse afterward.

The child has been named, and a new chapter begins for your dynasty. Great things may await your newest family member, though for now, their greatest achievement is having the entire household wrapped around their tiny finger.
Let the child rest
See your child!
A Name Has Been Chosen!
You Have Become A Parent
Rejoice!
Rat-infested food stores, contaminated water supply, sick-looking travelers… no one knows why or how, but many have suddenly fallen quite ill.
All persons affected: {ST_CHR_SIC}

The same question is on everyone's lips: what if the Black Death has returned? City officials helpfully remind everyone that {QUA_HYG_C}sanitation{##} is their own responsibility and prevention is the best cure.

You may want to {A_PHYCHE_C}visit a physician{##}, {A_PRASHR_C}pray{##} the sickness away, or at least use some salves or potions. Don't forget to check on the wellbeing of your workers and family members too, assuming you want your business and dynasty to survive this.
A Frightening Outbreak
Such tragedy. You had a wedding planned, and now it has turned into a funeral.
Not even Cyprian's book could save this courtship now.
Still, perhaps it was for the best. Whatever they had, it probably would not have produced good children anyway.
You tell yourself this with venom, because the alternative is admitting how dearly you would have loved them.
Your love was taken… by the Reaper
Until we meet again
You place a single flower upon their body and whisper the farewell you never had the chance to say.
Whether it is the first time or not, rejection hurts.
And unrequited love may be the cruelest of all: all that time spent hoping, waiting, and daydreaming of your first wedding night, only to see them now in the arms of another.
May they both catch a suspicious groin rash!
And so, you are alone again. Back to the tedious process of courtship.

How much easier it would be if one could simply receive, by pigeon mail, a neat little bundle of portraits, each with a short description of the person's qualities, flaws, wealth, and family connections.
Your love was taken
Life must go on

For a time, you still flinch whenever you hear their name. The portraits you had painted together remain tucked away where only you can find them. Eventually, they become little more than faded paint, and even more colorless memories.

As you walk the dark halls of your home, not able to fall sleep, you get the distinct feeling that you are being watched. You turn around suddenly and find a towering androgynous figure seemingly made of liquid swirling smoke.
Rather than threatening, the mysterious figure smiles knowingly and watches you attentively despite having no eyes to speak of. You feel it rummaging in the deepest corners of your mind.

No words are uttered, but your thoughts turn to an interesting but terrifying proposition: sacrifice a child of your body for the promise of a strong bloodline that will carry your dynasty into the annals of history. Make your choice now, mortal!
Deal with the Devil
Let it be such
With a satisfied nod, the mysterious figure fades away. As you blink and wonder whether you may have been dreaming, you hear the sudden screams of your spouse…
Exorcizamus te!
The mysterious figure hisses angrily and disappears in a puff of smoke. Deep down, you know it may return in your darkest hour.
Surely, you have heard that crime doesn't pay, yet you persisted in your wayward ways and now the day of reckoning has come. Better put your affairs in order while you still can.

Check that your named {CHAR_HEI_C}heir{##} is properly trained and worthy of carrying your {T_C}title{##} and taking over your {P_C}business{##}. You may even pass the mantle before the sentence is executed, to spare your family some shame.
As you stand on the gallows tomorrow, make sure that your last words are memorable for the right reasons.
Sentenced to Death!
I regret nothing!
Your execution is scheduled for tomorrow before noon. Use your remaining time wisely.
Some people think very highly of themselves and apparently wish to bestow this impression upon all others.

As such, you now find yourself challenged. Duels are an honor-bound tradition where the participants gain glory by engaging in elegant battle. Well, some refer to duels as a childish need to compensate for something, though they rarely mention for what. Others have even gone so far as to call for {CR_CRI_C}outlawing{##} duels.
In any case, if you decide to partake in such a ritual, make sure you are well equipped for the task. If not, perhaps a bruised ego is less painful than a stab in the belly.
Challenged to a Duel
The duel will start at sundown. Make sure you rest and regain your energy. You will need it.
Hopefully, you have enough energy to get through this duel in one piece.
Your opponent has decided to defend their honor.
You have exhibited both common sense and cowardice. Your public image may not survive though.
Your opponent has exhibited both common sense and cowardice. At least you've shamed them.
The bells toll to mark the tragedy of tragedies: the head of a dynasty exhales the last breath in empty halls. There is no one left to carry forth the family name.

War, disease, a predilection for gambling and, above all, a general dislike of conjugal duties have left this dynasty with no one to inherit the family business. Thus, all property reverts to the city.

If you're interested in acquiring production buildings at a bargain, better hurry and obtain the relevant license. But do not neglect your conjugal duties, or a similar fate may befall your own dynasty.
Dynasty Extinguished
Meditate upon the meaning of life
Breathe in… Hold… Breathe out… That's it.
As your final breath escapes your body, you let go of victories and regrets. The city lives on, indifferent to your plight, yet subtly shaped by your actions.

But just as your path dims, another may yet follow. Hopefully, you got your affairs in order well in advance, and your {CHAR_HEI_C}heir{##} is perfectly capable of taking over your {P_C}business{##} and {T_C}title{##}, ensuring your {CHAR_DYN_C}dynasty{##} thrives.

And so, your story ends, and your heir's begins. As the new head of the family, you have a will to attend to, a few words to say in your own favor, and perhaps some disappointed relatives whose goodwill can be bought.
They say time forgets nothing, yet remembers selectively. How long will your name linger in the memory of the city?
Your Time Has Come
Continue as your heir
Attend the Will Reading
The notary rolls up the will, gathers his papers, and declares the proceedings concluded. With the inheritance settled, there is nothing left to do but carry on.
For a moment, you find yourself wondering what the deceased would have thought of the way things turned out. Their legacy is now in your hands, along with all the responsibilities that come with it.
A lifetime of work, passed on with a few strokes of a quill. You can only hope to leave behind something equally worth inheriting.

To Play, Or Not to Play
Satisfied with the outcome?
It's all fun and games until someone gets caught.
Better safe than sorry.

Now, people are watching and tempers are flaring. Neither side wants to back down.
In case you have more {CHAR_ENE_C}energy{##} than sense, take your chance. You never know what comes out of it.
Not Every Action Needs a Reaction
Let fists speak
The fight was rough, and you walked away bruised. But in their anger, your opponent might have let slip a secret.
Insults were exchanged in a moment of tension, and a fight ensued. Too much was said and done, and it may be used against you one day.
Keep it civil
You answered with calm words, and your opponent was disarmed by your manners.
Despite a moment of tension when insults were exchanged and things almost got physical, your opponent showed sense and good manners.
Borrowed money and never returned it? Tried to bribe some official? Blackmailed fellow citizens? Did business too poorly for too long? Read the wrong books? Just be honest.

Haven't you ever heard that {CR_CRI_C}crime{##} doesn't pay? In fact, crime definitely pays, but not for you, it seems. You have been {CR_TRIPUN_C}sentenced{##} to jail time according to the {CR_SEV_C}severity of your crime{##} and how {L_LAWSEV_C}harsh{##} the current law is.
During your {ST_CHR_IMP_C}imprisonment{##}, your actions will be limited, so use this time wisely and learn from your mistakes.

The love of your life is ready to join you in the holy bond of matrimony. May your union be blessed with strong children to carry on your dynasty!
Wedding preparations will drain much energy, but your family and friends will rejoice with you, bearing gifts in celebration.
Alternatively, you may prefer a frugal event. In that case, better be prepared for meager wedding gifts and a cooler embrace by your new spouse.
The Wedding Day
Blessed be this union!
Attend Your Wedding
Your wedding banquet is all people talk about these days.
An upstanding citizen threw a wedding banquet and those who attended just can't stop talking about it.
Just get on with it
Hopefully, your spouse learns to manage expectations better than you manage your finances.
The guests have gathered, the priest is waiting, and your beloved is dressed for the occasion. Make your way to the high altar, exchange your vows, and seal your union before God and your witnesses.
After that, you may find a few other ways to enjoy the festivities. A wedding is a celebration, after all!
One Last Wedding Expense

The festivities are finally drawing to a close. The last guests are making their way home, some a little less steadily than others, though a few seem determined to accompany you all the way to the marriage bed. Such enthusiasm for your union!
Once you've finally secured a moment alone, your new spouse suggests taking a little journey together. A honeymoon, just the two of you, away from the demands of family and business.
It would certainly cost a pretty penny, but the time spent together could strengthen your marriage. And a happy marriage may well improve your chances of welcoming a few heirs into the family!
Enjoy a Honeymoon
Just the Two of Us
The honeymoon costs a small fortune, but the time spent together brings you closer than ever.
Settle Into Married Life
Home, Not So Sweet Home
You may have saved a small fortune, but the embrace you receive tonight is noticeably colder. Perhaps some things are worth spending a little coin on.
This morning, at one of the town's mines, a support frame collapsed, burying the crew beneath it. The tragedy shook the entire city.
Last Shift
Lives were lost. The town sends prayers and comfort to their families in this dark hour.
From the shadows of an alley, a beggar raises his hand toward you. Do you have anything to offer?
You never know what may come of it. Beggars live by scavenging and might reward your generosity with an item, a piece of evidence… or nothing at all.
The Beggar
Offer money
The beggar takes your coin with a nod, then ducks into a crowd. No more is seen or heard of him.
From the folds of his ragged cloak, he presses a small vial into your hand. No word of thanks, only a steady gaze before he turns away.
Offer help
The beggar presses a folded note into your hand. Its lines point to another's secret dealings — enough to be used as evidence against them.
Do nothing
You ignore him. He chuckles as if he knew your choice all along. By the time you look back, the alley is empty.
Can you believe those fellows at the bar today? No? You did not hear them?
Well, I have made a habit of keeping my ears open. It is good for business — and considerably cheaper than paying a spy.

You see that poor man with the swollen face? And the well-dressed fellow beside him? That second man used to be a small-time merchant. Then fortune smiled upon him, and he decided that earning money was less profitable than charging other people to hear how he had done it.
Apparently, he told our unfortunate friend that honey would be the town's next great fortune. Men will believe almost anything if the advice comes from fine clothes and costs enough.
The bees disagreed.
Still, all this talk has left me craving mead. Queen bees can be found in the Timberlands. Go find one, and we shall see whether that merchant was onto something after all.
I spent the morning waiting for a mason to finish a sanding block. He arranged his tools, inspected the workbench, and then stood there looking thoughtful.
We had no stone.

Before your workers can craft anything, the required materials must be in the storeroom. Send your cart to the Marketplace to buy what they need, or visit Resource Sites such as mines, where materials are often available at better prices because they come straight from the source.
Once the materials are unloaded, production can begin. Potential is just another word for empty shelves.
Your workshop is coming along nicely. Now, I did not want to say anything, but what about the rest of your life?
There are a few respectable unmarried people in Herle. I know which are kind, which are sensible, and which only pretend to be either. A lady has an intuition for these things.
Find someone you like, court them properly, and perhaps marriage will follow.
I am not interfering. I am helping.
You are the new smith. Marta said you would be here.

I'm Elsbeth, the town's mason. I collect old swords, though the fittings interest me more than the blades. Blades receive all the praise. Fittings hold everything together and are only noticed when they fail.
You should probably begin with those. Craft some fittings and sell them at the marketplace. Someone will need them soon, even if they do not know it yet.
Keep one for yourself. A sword begins with smaller things.
After finishing your errands, you sit for a moment and watch the town pass by.

A merchant argues over the price of wool. A boy steals an apple, then immediately drops it while trying to look innocent. Nearby, two women complain that their husbands somehow become helpless the moment a chair needs moving.
Herle is alive.
Then you notice two men standing at a distance, making a great effort not to be noticed… and failing badly. You recognize one of them as a town official.
The other man slips a purse into the official's belt pouch. They shake hands and quickly part ways.
A folded note falls to the ground behind them.
When you retrieve it, you find the amount of the payment written inside, followed by the words: “Do not forget to vote for me.”
The fool even signed his name.
Someone broke into my joinery.
I switched to selling from my storefront to avoid robbers on the road. It turns out they were willing to walk the rest of the way.
You wouldn't happen to know how to install barred windows, would you? No? A pity. You certainly wouldn't be short of clients.
Apparently, since the authorities cannot protect the streets themselves, they have decided to leave the work to whichever desperate citizens are willing to put their lives on the line.
I hear guard service pays well. Hm… I shall recommend it to someone I dislike.
I once employed the finest brewer I ever met. He could brew a full batch in half the time it took most men, without sacrificing a drop of quality.
Unfortunately, whenever I sent him to serve the tables, he frightened half the customers into drinking elsewhere. Excellent with barrels. Terrible with people.
That taught me to hire workers for what they are good at. Some have the hands for crafting, some can sell anything placed before them, and some know how to keep customers happy.
As a smith, you should look for those skilled in handicraft, choose someone who suits your needs, and hire them. If you are happy with the workers you have, you can train their skills.
skip
You linger, admiring the stonework, as though it alone were the handiwork of God. Yet His truest work is found in the faithful gathered here — and it is the duty of a skilled priest to guide them.

I am Bishop van Hochstaden-Herle. People come here carrying the consequences of what they failed to notice, correct, or prevent. They call such failures misfortune. More often, they are simply neglect allowed to mature.

Your workers may stand at the forge, but their failures will still bear your name. If you cannot recognize waste, clumsy work, or lost time, then you are not directing them. You are merely paying them.
Improve your handicraft. Capable workers are valuable, but a capable master makes them better. You need not perform every task yourself—but do not mistake ignorance for delegation.
I have been watching you. Not closely. Closely enough.
Your work no longer looks like the work of a beginner. I think you are ready to seek a higher master grade.
It will bring renown to your name. A higher mastery will let you accomplish more in your profession and, in time, build a larger smithy offering more crafts and services.
It is curious how skill takes up no room, yet always seems to require a larger building.
What is that you are holding? Let me see… reading Hm. This looks like evidence.

Let me be clear: what happens in my inn stays in my inn. People need somewhere they can speak freely, make fools of themselves, and return the next day without discovering that half the town knows about it.
But you found this elsewhere, so it is no concern of mine. You may sell the evidence, use it for blackmail, or take it before the court. If you want the law involved, press charges.
What you do after that is between you, your conscience, and whoever pays best.
Oh, there you are! Come, you must meet the family before one of them wanders off.
This is Jan, Willem, Pieter, Margriet, Lijsbeth, Cornelis, Aleid, Geertruid, little Hendrika — and the one hiding beneath the table is Adriaan. Unless that is Pieter. No, Pieter is eating the cheese.
Ah, my little blessings.

A business may fill your purse, and a title may raise your standing, but an heir gives all that work somewhere to go. Someone to carry the family name, inherit what you have built, and perhaps improve upon it.
You should think about starting a family of your own. A little private time with your spouse is often where such things begin.
My family had produced priests for generations, and they had every intention of producing one more. I had other plans, though I did not know what they were yet.

So I left home and travelled through Bohemia. Somewhere along the way, I discovered brewing. Shortly after that, I discovered the woman who would become my wife. One proved far more patient with me than the other.
Loving a trade, however, does not make it yours. Before I could keep an inn, I had to present myself to the Innkeepers' Guild and learn the profession properly.
The guilds are the place to go when you wish to take up a new profession. They also offer professional training, which can bring you closer to the rank of master in your trade.
Changing one's path is not always easy. Still, I have found it preferable to spending a lifetime walking in the wrong direction.
What happened last night? While you slept, the whole city seems to have gone mad, and now no one remembers a thing.
Fabian's pilgrim badges were stolen, fires were set, and moustaches were painted on every noble portrait in the town hall.
Was it some kind of purge? What on earth happened?
Evidence is everywhere, and some of your own memories already contain it. The only question is who will make use of it first.
The Purge
What has come over everyone? The townsfolk are seized by an itching need to cause trouble, as though a little destruction were necessary to endure another day.
The town crier has announced the Purge. By decree of the highest officials, one day of disorder shall preserve order for all the rest.

Goodwife Gertrud was seen beating the man who trampled her flowers last week. Children are vandalizing buildings, politicians are telling the truth, and Ruprecht, the robber, has somehow got his hands on a very dangerous book.
Today, no one is afraid.
The Purge
Unfortunately, it was all a misunderstanding. The officials have withdrawn the decree and insist that everyone may still be prosecuted for their crimes.
There is now an impressive amount of evidence documenting the town's misconduct.
The only question is who will take advantage of it first.
The Aftermath
I was passing by when your building caught my eye. It is wearing in several places, though not enough for most people to notice. That is how damage likes to begin — quietly.
The mortar is loosening, and one of the cracks has already begun to spread. Leave it much longer, and the repair will become a far larger job.

Were it mine, I would repair it now. A poorly maintained building affects every part of a business — customer appeal, productivity, sanitation, and safety. Neglect has a way of making itself expensive.
Marta says I worry too much about cracks. Marta works with wood.
Certain things are told to a priest because they cannot be safely told to a master. I will not say who spoke to me, nor repeat what was said.
But you should know this: a generous wage does not excuse poor treatment, and kind words do not make up for an empty purse. Your workers care about both how they are paid and how they are treated.
See to one, and they may tolerate you. See to both, and they may remain loyal.
Ah! A face I don't know! That does not happen often in my inn. I'm Hendrik Bloudil. You must be the new smith.
I hope you have a better head for business than the last one. He was too fond of his cups and not fond enough of his accounts.
Still, as we say: the inn fills the cup, and the church empties the conscience. Drink tonight, pray tomorrow, and wake as good as new.

I admit, I do not follow the second half as faithfully as I once did. In Prague, I heard a preacher speak as though a man's faith should be measured by how he lives, not by how often he crosses a church threshold. I found some sense in that.
Even so, you should pay the church a visit. You can hardly claim to know Herle until you have stood beneath its tower.
You will not believe what happened on my way here.
Robbers ambushed my cart and took an entire cartload of crossbows. Crossbows! So now I have lost a fortune, and the local criminals are considerably better armed.
I should have hired escorts. I knew that, of course.

Do be careful inside the walls as well, especially when carrying anything valuable. You can sell goods from your storefront, naturally, but the Marketplace is much faster. Though speed loses some of its charm when your cart never arrives.
For the moment, I think I shall trust my storefront. I am still one step ahead of those robbers. They will see.
A de Rochefort has nothing to discuss with a mere commoner.
I value my time. You should learn to value yours.
Claim the title of Burgher, and perhaps then we shall have business together. Until that day, do not waste either.
God be praised, the smithy has a smith again! You must be the newcomer. Welcome to town. I'm Marta, the town's joiner — and, before you ask, yes, I already have work in mind for you.

My twin sister, Elsbeth, is the town's mason. You'll likely meet her soon enough. She is something of a collector, though she can be rather particular about what deserves keeping. She asks unusual questions, too, and has an uncanny habit of already knowing half the answer.
Pay it no mind. Elsbeth may be peculiar company, but she is good company. Between her curiosity and my need for hinges, I doubt we shall leave you lonely for long.
Still, if you wish to meet more of the town, visit the Inn. Hendrik keeps the place, and he is one of the kindest men you are likely to meet.
For now, acquaint yourself with your new workshop. I'll give you a little time before I begin arriving with requests.

A Dynasty Head has been convicted of a notorious crime. 

You may spend your energy to voice an opinion — or mind your own business. 

Remember: the enemy of my enemy is my friend.

A Dynasty Head has been convicted of a notorious crime. Shocking, really. They seemed like such a fine citizen: Sunday prayers, taxes paid on time, always ready to help others — well, as long as those others could offer something in return. But then again, God made hierarchy for a reason.
Well, it is the talk of the town, and this is your chance to take part. You may spend your energy to voice an opinion or save it for worthier pursuits.
Some people make friends by hating the same person, or you could try to defend them instead — extra points if they can return the favor later.

Always remember: the only certainties in life are death and taxes, and death only comes once. Taxes come, or rather go, at the end of every year. If you can't pay, you better hope that you can make up for it while {ST_CHR_IMP_C}imprisoned{##}.
